title: The Unofficial Playlist
premise: Cyrus Hartwell, a seventeen-year-old coder, has spent two years running an anonymous account that exposes the small cruelties of his elite prep school—until a college essay prompt ('Describe a moment you couldn't stay silent') cracks his armor and the account's voice starts bleeding into his real one. When his best friend Dev is expelled for a cheating scandal Cyrus knows was engineered by legacy student Grant Whitmore, Cyrus must choose between protecting his anonymity and testifying with proof he can only get by winning the school's hackathon championship—and then the regional coding finals that Grant's family is bankrolling. In the end, Cyrus wins the championship that matters (the truth), loses the one that doesn't (the trophy), and walks into prom with Dev, having learned that inheritance isn't what's left to you—it's what you choose to carry forward.
about_author: Theo Hartwell is the pseudonym of a former debate coach and amateur archivist who grew up in a town where one family owned the newspaper, the bank, and most of the silence. They write stories about teenagers who refuse to be quiet, and they still check the library card catalog for messages.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine, Obviously
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. He narrates his meticulously ordinary life while secretly posting as @hollowoaktruth, exposing a teacher's grade-selling. The emotional beat is the thrill and terror of a double life, ending with a college essay prompt that makes his stomach drop: 'Describe a moment you couldn't stay silent.'

chapters.title: The Question Nobody Can Stop Answering
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. In AP English, students read their essay drafts aloud; classmate Wren's raw honesty about her brother's overdose stuns the room. Cyrus writes a draft he immediately deletes—then can't stop rewriting. Emotional beat: the prompt as a splinter working toward the surface.

chapters.title: Dev Okafor, Human Sunlamp
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev, Cyrus's best friend since seventh grade, balances tutoring, track, and caring for his grandmother. He notices Cyrus flinching at his phone but doesn't push. Emotional beat: warmth and loyalty, and the quiet cost of being the friend who always gives.

chapters.title: Legacy
chapters.summary: Grant Whitmore's POV. Grant, third-generation Whitmore, feels the weight of his family's donations as a debt he can never repay, so he collects favors instead. He leans on a teacher to adjust his transcript. Emotional beat: entitlement as fear wearing a letterman jacket.

chapters.title: The Account Knows Too Much
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. @hollowoaktruth's follower count explodes after a post about the cheating ring on the debate team. Cyrus starts receiving DMs begging him to investigate Whitmore family 'scholarships.' Emotional beat: power intoxicating and isolating at once.

chapters.title: Wren Reads the Room
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Sharp-eyed Wren, the school paper's editor, notices the anonymous account's posting schedule matches a certain someone's free period. She says nothing—but starts her own file. Emotional beat: curiosity sharpening into suspicion, and admiration she resents.

chapters.title: Hackathon Sign-Ups
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The annual Hartwell-Whitmore Hackathon opens; the prize includes a direct line to the regional coding finals and a Whitmore family endowment interview. Cyrus and Dev team up. Emotional beat: hope, and the irony that the family name is on the trophy.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev and Cyrus plan their project—a peer tutoring platform—while Dev confesses he needs the endowment interview to afford college at all. Emotional beat: the friendship's unspoken imbalance surfacing gently.

chapters.title: The Essay Draft That Burns
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus writes his college essay about the account without naming it, and Ms. Ferreira's comment—'This is the truest thing you've written; why is it hiding?'—keeps him up all night. Emotional beat: being seen before he's ready.

chapters.title: Grant's Offer
chapters.summary: Grant's POV. Grant offers Dev a spot on his hackathon team—better resources, guaranteed win—making clear it's a loyalty test aimed at Cyrus. Emotional beat: a bribe dressed as generosity, and Grant's flicker of genuine loneliness.

chapters.title: Dev Says Yes
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Cornered by his grandmother's mounting medical bills, Dev accepts Grant's offer, hating himself. He doesn't tell Cyrus why. Emotional beat: shame, and love making the wrong choice for the right reasons.

chapters.title: The Silence Between Friends
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus learns Dev switched teams from a group chat screenshot. He says nothing, posting instead a blistering anonymous thread about 'friends who sell out.' Emotional beat: hurt curdling into hypocrisy he can't see.

chapters.title: The Cheating Scandal
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Answer keys surface; Dev is caught with one on his phone the morning of midterms. The evidence is airtight—too airtight. Emotional beat: the horror of watching a frame-up assemble in real time.

chapters.title: Expulsion Hearing
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The disciplinary committee, chaired by a Whitmore family trustee, expels Dev in eleven minutes. Cyrus almost speaks—almost—and doesn't. Emotional beat: the specific shame of silence when it costs someone else.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev tells his grandmother the truth; she says, 'They took your name. Don't let them take your story.' Emotional beat: grief met with dignity, and the seed of the fight to come.

chapters.title: The Prompt Answers Back
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus submits a college essay that is, essentially, a confession in code—a description of @hollowoaktruth without the handle. Emotional beat: the first true sentence he's written in two years.

chapters.title: Wren's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren confronts Cyrus with her evidence of his double life and her own: she's traced the answer-key leak to Grant's group chat but needs a source inside to prove it. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance, two keepers of secrets recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Plan That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus realizes the hackathon's systems—the submission logs, the proctoring software—are the same ones that 'caught' Dev. Winning means access. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the championship becomes a lockpick.

chapters.title: Rebuilding the Team
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Cyrus asks Dev—still expelled, still allowed to compete as an independent per the handbook's fine print—to team up again. Dev makes him say the real reason out loud. Emotional beat: forgiveness as a door held open, not given.

chapters.title: Training Montage, Sort Of
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The trio—Cyrus, Dev, Wren—build their project in Wren's garage: a transparency tool that timestamps and verifies document provenance. It's literally the technology that could expose the frame-up. Emotional beat: joy of making something true together.

chapters.title: Grant Doubles Down
chapters.summary: Grant's POV. Grant learns Wren is investigating and panics, escalating from favors to forgery with his father's lawyer's quiet help. Emotional beat: the moment a lie requires infrastructure.

chapters.title: The DM That Changes Everything
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. An anonymous message to @hollowoaktruth: 'I was in the room. I can prove Dev was set up. Meet me.' Signed with a debate-team in-joke. Emotional beat: hope arriving disguised as a trap.

chapters.title: The Informant
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The informant is Priya, a Whitmore scholarship student who watched the answer key being planted. She's terrified; the endowment pays her rent. Emotional beat: the price of loyalty when loyalty is a paycheck.

chapters.title: Midnight in the Server Room
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus and Priya retrieve the audit logs from the hackathon's archive server—technically against the rules, arguably not against the law. They're nearly caught by security. Emotional beat: heart-pounding transgression, justice outside the law.

chapters.title: The Logs Don't Lie
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The logs show the answer key was uploaded to Dev's cloud account from a device registered to Grant—three hours before Dev's phone ever touched it. Emotional beat: vindication so sharp it hurts.

chapters.title: Hollow Oak Truth, Final Post
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus drafts the post that would expose everything—and realizes posting it burns Priya's safety and his own future. Emotional beat: the account's purpose and peril finally in the same sentence.

chapters.title: Hackathon Prelims
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The trio's provenance tool dominates the preliminary round, unnerving the Whitmore-funded judges. Grant's team accuses them of 'an agenda.' Emotional beat: excellence as provocation.

chapters.title: The Trustee's Warning
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The Whitmore family trustee offers Cyrus a full-ride endowment if he withdraws and hands over his 'sources.' He declines with his heart hammering. Emotional beat: the bribe he can't afford to refuse, refused.

chapters.title: Priya Breaks
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Grant's lawyer confronts Priya; her scholarship is threatened. She goes dark, deleting her messages. Emotional beat: the machinery of silence grinding a good person down.

chapters.title: Everything Falls Apart
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Without Priya, the logs are inadmissible; the school rejects Dev's appeal. Cyrus blames himself; he and Dev fight for real. Emotional beat: the lowest point, loyalty stretched to snapping.

chapters.title: The Essay Prompt, Again
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Rereading his own college essay, Cyrus finds the answer he's been dodging: he doesn't need to stay anonymous to be safe—he needs to be honest to be free. Emotional beat: the turn; fear reorganizing into resolve.

chapters.title: Regional Finals Announcement
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The trio qualifies for the regional coding finals, televised, with the Whitmore endowment board in attendance. Wren proposes the insane plan: demo the tool live, on the real audit logs, as the project's use case. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration shaking hands.

chapters.title: Assembling the Proof
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus, Dev, and Wren spend a feverish week verifying everything—device registrations, timestamps, Priya's recovered backup drive she'd hidden in the library. Emotional beat: quiet, methodical courage.

chapters.title: Priya Comes Back
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya watches Dev's grandmother speak at a school board meeting about second chances, and decides her rent isn't worth her soul. She agrees to testify on record. Emotional beat: a small person choosing to be enormous.

chapters.title: The Finals
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. On stage at regionals, mid-demo, Cyrus abandons the script and shows the judges the audit logs proving the frame-up, live, naming no one but letting the timestamps speak. The room detonates. Emotional beat: the climax—truth performed in public, unanonymous at last.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The judges disqualify the team for 'misuse of competition data.' Grant's team wins the trophy. Nobody in the crowd is watching the trophy. Emotional beat: losing the prize and winning the point, gloriously.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The school board, the newspaper (Wren's front page), and eventually the state's education office take up the case; the trustee resigns; Dev's expulsion is overturned. Grant, facing his father's cold fury, is left alone with what he built. Emotional beat: consequences arriving unevenly but undeniably.

chapters.title: What Grant Carries
chapters.summary: Grant's POV. Grant, stripped of his inherited future, writes his own college essay about the moment he couldn't stop lying. It's the first honest thing he's ever made. Emotional beat: not redemption exactly—just the door left unlocked.

chapters.title: Prom, Unanonymous
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus posts his final @hollowoaktruth entry—a goodbye and a handoff—then deletes the account from the gym floor, phone in hand, while Dev and Wren drag him toward the dance. Emotional beat: lightness; the mask coming off like a splinter finally out.

chapters.title: The Inheritance
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, epilogue-style. At graduation, Cyrus reads his published essay aloud—the one about staying silent—and hands the mic to Dev. He's accepted to college not on the endowment but on the essay Ms. Ferreira wouldn't let him hide. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined as truth carried forward, and passed on.
